Absolutely—this is a big, personal choice, and you deserve advice that respects the significance of what you’re about to do. Since you already have the date set, the focus is on style and placement to make it feel right for both of you and for you in the years to come.

Below are some ideas you can consider (and keep in mind that getting a few sketches from a professional tattoo artist will help refine the look before you commit).

### Lettering Styles (with a quick “pros/cons” rundown)

| Style | Look & Feel | Legibility at Large Scale | Best For… |
|-------|--------------|---------------------------|-----------|
| **Block/Caps (Bold Block Letters)** | Clean, strong, modern, straightforward | ★★★★★ (very legible) | If you want something instantly recognizable and timeless. Good for large, bold names. |
| **Script/Cursive (Handwritten Style)** | Flowing, artistic, intimate | ★★★☆☆ (can be tricky at big size) | If you want a more personal, fluid vibe—perhaps with flourishes that echo her personality. |
| **Old English / Blackletter** | Gothic, vintage, dramatic | ★★☆☆☆ (harder to read at size) | If the vibe of medieval or classic “tattoo” aesthetics appeals to you—just be aware it may age differently on skin. |
| **Outline or “Negative Space”** | Edgy, striking, modern | ★★★☆☆ (can be legible if outlines are wide) | Great for a subtle, “effortless” look—good if you want the name to pop visually without heavy shading. |
| **Hybrid (Block letters with subtle cursive details)** | Balanced, unique | ★★★★☆ (fairly legible) | A good compromise: block readability + her personality in the flourishes. |

**Takeaway:** Since the tattoo will be “big letters” and **visible every day**, a **block or bold modern style** will likely give the most legible, dependable result while still feeling powerful and intentional.

### Placement Ideas

1. **Inner Forearm (just below the elbow)**
   - **Pros:** Easy to see when you extend your arm forward (e.g., typing, reaching). Less likely to get “caught” in casual display unless you deliberately stretch your arm upward.
   - **Cons:** A bit more “hidden” in many social photos unless you pose it deliberately.

2. **Outer Forearm (near the wrist)**
   - **Pros:** Very easy to photograph and display when you raise your arm; a universal attention‑grabbing spot.
   - **Cons:** More likely to be part of everyday views (hands up when waving, gesturing, etc.).

3. **Upper Forearm (above the elbow)**
   - **Pros:** A classic “forearm” location that works for hand‑held photos, etc.
   - **Cons:** Similar visibility pros/cons as above; some people find the upper forearm a little more permanent‑feeling.

**Tip:** Ask your chosen artist to sketch a small version on your skin or on paper so you can see how the size and spacing feel as the tattoo grows.

### Extra Things to Consider Before You Commit

- **Letter spacing & proportions:** Thin letters can get lost at large scale; make sure the spacing balances readability with visual impact.
- **Cone healing:** A big, solid‑color tattoo can be a bit more noticeable while it heals, so consider a style that hides a bit of scabbing if you’re sensitive to post‑care visibility.
- **Removal possibility (just in case):** If you ever feel uncertain later, block/caps are easiest to remove or cover up because they’re more defined.
- **Long‑term skin aging:** Keep in mind that forearm skin can be more exposed to sun, which can affect ink longevity. You might consider UV‑protective products or future touch‑ups if needed.

---

#### Quick Action Plan

1. **Consult a local artist** – Bring a list of names (including spacing/typographic preferences) and ask them to sketch a few style variations on paper.
2. **Choose the sketch you love** – First iteration is fine; many artists can refine it to match your ideas.
3. **Decide final location** – Walk through a day imagining how you’d pose your arm (work, hang‑ing out, social media photos) and see which spot feels most authentic to both of you.
4. **Lock in size** – Big letters will be more dramatic—make sure the spacing is generous enough for each initial or letter to breathe.
5. **Post‑care** – Follow the artist’s after‑care instructions carefully; forearm tattoos heal faster than many areas, but keep the skin moisturized and protected from harsh UV exposure.

If you want to mention the actual name (or at least the first few letters) or share any preferences you have (e.g., “more decorative flourishing” vs. “minimalist”), let me know and I can tailor the suggestions further! Good luck—may the ink be as lasting as the love you feel.
